messages:
leo: Heads-up: ops asked whether autofallback rollouts should respect customer quotas and billing caps. If we route to a larger model or reroute to dedicated instances, costs change. Need policy UX decisions.

maria: Yes we need boundaries. Autofallback should never exceed the quota/billing-backstop for the tenant. Fallback action must be vetoed if it would blow the customer's soft cap.

priya: Proposal: policy actions carry a "cost_estimate" field so the console can preview cost delta before enabling an action. If cost_estimate > tenant.remaining_budget -> action disabled (unless operator override).

dave: Add to that: a "billing_backstop" flag that says whether a tenant-level override is allowed by RBAC. Enterprise customers might want different behavior.

katie: UX: in the rollout editor show a small inline cost bar: projected monthly delta at current traffic. Also show worst-case delta if autoscale kicks.

leo: Good. Also we need to decide telemetry tags. When autofallback fires, tag metrics with policy_id, decision_reason, and quota_state so we can pivot dashboards.

maria: For auditability, capture the effective budget check: {checked_at, remaining_budget, projected_delta}. We should store that as text in the audit snapshot.

priya: Implementation detail: runtime will call quota service _synchronously_ during decision path. That adds latency — we should cache quota checks for 15s and evaluate TTL miss policies. Add an option: "defer_quota_check": true to allow fallback and then reconcile, but that seems risky.

dave: I prefer conservative approach: synchronous check by default. Defer option only for non-bill-impacting soft_degrade templates.

leo: What about the operator override? We need a one-click "allow cost exceed" with justification and TTL. That should create an audit event and notify billing slack channel.

katie: Microcopy: button label "Override quota for this decision" and modal asks for reason + expiry (default 1h). Must be RBAC-gated.

priya: For templates, we'll add template-level budget metadata. Example template snippet (shown as text in editor):

---
name: availability_saver
action: route_to_fallback_model
cost_estimate: "+0.04 USD/1000 tokens"
budget_impact: "low"
requires_quota_check: "true"
---

leo: Nice. Also we need a replay feature that simulates the decision against a historic trace but respecting current quota state and billing rules (so we can predict false positives).

maria: Playback should accept a toggle: live_quota (current remaining budget) vs original_quota (snapshot at decision). This helps root-cause whether a fallback was quota-driven.

dave: On notifications: hard_degrade + quota_override -> page oncall and billing team. soft_degrade only creates an info event in rollout timeline.

katie: Add an "explain" panel that shows the signal waterfall: p95 latency, backend_error_rate, quota_check, cost_estimate. Each row collapsible with raw numbers.

priya: Edge case: multiple policies fire for same route. Runtime must resolve by priority then by estimated cost impact (prefer cheaper action). We'll expose tie-breaker policy: priority, then cost.

leo: Ok action items: priya implement cost_estimate plumbing + quota check sync cache. dave add RBAC override endpoint. katie update console mockups with cost bar, override modal, and explain panel. maria to write microcopy + ops playbook (what to do when fallback fires and billing override happened).

deploy-bot: policy "availability_saver" draft created by leo at 1771000001.

leo: Thanks all — planning to start a small canary with only non-bill-impacting soft_degrades tomorrow. Will post link to PR and mockups. Ping me if you want to be on the review.
